Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 9(b) contains a genuine express performance warranty from Kubient that exceeds the preferred position on the two material terms. Scope: the Service "will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)), services will "be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)), no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)), and compliance with all applicable Laws "now and throughout the Term" (9(b)(ix)). Duration: the warranties are drafted as continuing representations, warranties and covenants for the whole Term rather than being cut off after 12 months/90 days, so the period is better than preferred. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so this is not walk-away "AS IS" territory. The only preferred element absent is a stated repair/replace/refund remedy sentence; we note but do not flag this, because leaving the warranty to general contract remedies (plus the 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b) and indemnity for breach of warranty under 11(a)(iv)) preserves broader relief for us than a vendor-elected, typically exclusive, repair-replace-refund remedy would.

payload.text: 4. Term and Termination.

(a) The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement, (b) Either Party may terminate this Agreement if the other Party commits a material breach of the Agreement and upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party, such other Party hasn't cured the breach within such thirty (30) days. Either Party may terminate the Agreement immediately if the other party (i) becomes insolvent or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;

(ii) suffers or permits the appointment of a conservator or receiver for its business or assets or any similar action by a governmental entity for the purpose of assuming operation or control of the Party due to the financial condition of the Party;

(iii) becomes subject to any proceeding under any bankruptcy or insolvency law whether domestic or foreign and such proceeding or action has not been dismissed within a sixty (60) period; or (iv) has wound up or liquidated its business, voluntarily or otherwise.
(c) Upon termination of the Agreement:
(i) Kubient will cease providing the Services;
(ii) the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked, (iii) Customer will promptly cease use of the Services and the Auction Platform;
(iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.

5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit. Unless specified otherwise in an Exhibit, Kubient shall be responsible for contracting with all advertisers, agencies, media buyers, and/or sponsors (collectively "Advertisers") on Customer's behalf, including Advertisers with whom Customer has existing relationships. Pursuant to the doctrine of sequential liability, payment from Kubient to Customer shall be made within seven (7) days from Kubient's receipt of payment, regardless of when Customer submits an invoice. Customer acknowledges and agrees that Kubient shall proceed with recovery of the amounts due on a best effort basis but will not initiate any legal action against a delinquent party without the express written consent and support of Customer. Except of taxes associated with Kubient's income, Customer shall be responsible for paying all applicable sales, use or other taxes, duties, or tariffs applicable to its use of the Services.

Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Title: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer
Kind: direction

Severity: high
Category: commercial

Position — fallback:
Early-termination fee capped at 3 months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Detection guidance:

Redline guidance:
Delete the Customer-payable LD; if an early-termination fee is unavoidable, cap it at 3 months' fees.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum-fee obligation payable by AP, which matches the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages). Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "minimum", and termination/fee language return nothing of that kind. The only termination-payment language (paragraph 4(a)) entitles Kubient to "all fees generated during the termination period" — under the revenue-share model in paragraph 5 these are amounts generated from Advertisers and paid by Kubient to AP, not a sum AP pays out, so it is not a Customer-payable liquidated amount. Note for context that fee terms sit in Exhibits not included here; if any Exhibit adds an early-termination or shortfall payment by AP, it should be capped at three months' fees per the fallback. No redline required.

Category: insurance
Position — preferred:

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the General Provisions (Section 14, p0063–p0073) contain no coverage or certificate-of-insurance requirement. Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per its own warranty at p0035, collects, maintains and stores visitor data, so it is squarely a services/hosting vendor touching our data — the walk-away scenario of no insurance for a vendor processing personal data. We therefore insert a short insurance covenant at the preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request) as new Section 14(j), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, committed spend, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on AP. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return only the Winning Bid Price floor set by AP itself (p0014, which benefits us) and Kubient's disclaimer that no minimum revenue level is guaranteed (p0062) — neither is a commitment binding AP. **Finding submitted: missing (medium severity), confidence 0.86.**

**What I found.** Section 4(c) (paras p0019–p0022) is the Agreement's only effect-of-termination provision. It covers cessation of Services, revocation of the licence, AP's cessation of use, and a mutual "return **or destroy**" option for Confidential Information. There is:

- no transition/migration assistance obligation on Kubient;
- no right for AP to receive its Content, Requests or other platform data back in a usable format;
- no deletion certification.

Targeted searches for transition/migration/export/retrieval language returned nothing elsewhere; "Customer Data" is not a defined term in the document.

**Why it fails the fallback.** Because Kubient may elect to *destroy* rather than return, the clause sits at or near the playbook's walk-away position (no data return / immediate deletion) and does not reach even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New paragraph 4(c)(v) inserted after p0022 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, then deletion with written certification — with an express override of 4(c)(iv)'s destroy option for Customer Data, so the new right cannot be defeated by the existing clause. The comment offers the 90-day fallback if the six-month period is resisted.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.

Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Section 4(c) is the only effect-of-termination provision: Kubient ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, Customer stops using the Auction Platform, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election. Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer / AP) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Kubient Master Services Agreement dated 5 February 
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Thirteen clauses are compliant, three are deviations requiring redlines, and three rules have no usable clause in the document at all.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the areas that usually cause the most trouble. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no non-solicit and no audit right running against us; Section 1 expressly confirms we remain free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. The vendor-side indemnity at Section 11 is broad, procedurally sound and uncapped in practice, and the Section 9(b) performance warranty runs for the whole Term, which is better than our preferred position. Assignment, termination for convenience and governing law all sit at or above the fallback and are not redlined.

Three issues need to be raised with the counterparty. First, and most significant, Section 7 waives consequential damages but contains **no monetary cap of any kind**, leaving our direct liability unlimited; because this is a revenue-share deal in which we pay no fees to Kubient, a "fees paid" cap would be illusory, so we propose the greater-of formulation with a USD 1,000,000 floor plus standard uncapped carve-outs. Second, the Section 2 platform licence is expressly "revocable" without qualifier and runs to Customer alone, with Section 6(a) barring third-party access absent Kubient's prior written consent — so Affiliates and contractors are excluded and the licence could be pulled at will. Third, the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, which exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling.

Three rules are unaddressed: there is no IP/ownership article allocating our Content, Requests or visitor data; Section 4(c) permits each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information with no transition assistance or data-return right; and there is no insurance covenant at all, notwithstanding that Kubient hosts the platform and, on its own warranty, collects and stores visitor data.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Section 11) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (Section 14(h)) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 4(a), 5) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (Sections 2, 6(a)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (law at fallback) | Preamble (Section 14(a)) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 4(c)) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (exceeds preferred) | Preamble (Sections 9(b), 13) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 14) |

### Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**LOL-CAP (critical, deviation — Section 7).** Section 7 is a mutual consequential-damages waiver carved out for indemnification and breach of confidentiality, but no cap on direct liability appears anywhere in the document. The fallback requires a mutual 12-months'-fees cap with carve-outs, so the total absence of a cap fails on a material term. Our redline adds a mutual cap on the preferred greater-of basis using amounts paid or payable between the Parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, adds the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirms revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" for cap purposes. The existing mutual waiver is acceptable and is left intact.

**LICENSE (high, deviation — Sections 2 and 6(a)).** The grant is expressly "revocable" with no qualifier, so on its face Kubient may withdraw the licence at will mid-Term, and it runs to "Customer" alone while Section 6(a) bars third-party access without Kubient's prior written consent — leaving Affiliate and contractor access to Kubient's discretion, contrary to the fallback (Affiliates covered on written notice). Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirms such access is not prohibited third-party access (with us responsible for their compliance), and limits revocation to expiration or termination under Section 4. Successor transfer is already handled by Section 14(h) and is preserved.

**RENEWAL (medium, deviation — Section 4(a)).** Renewal terms are successive one-year periods, which is acceptable, but the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. Our redline shortens the notice to 30 days and confirms it may be exercised as a non-renewal election; we can settle at 60 days. Pricing is a revenue share with no unilateral uplift mechanic, so the CPI/3% cap is not engaged.

**IP (high, missing).** There is no ownership article. The only ownership-adjacent language is Kubient's warranty that it owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and products delivered, our warranty that we own the Content and Properties, and a trademark-only provision — none of which allocates ownership of our Content, Requests or visitor data, assigns deliverables, or excludes joint ownership, while Kubient collects and stores visitor data and receives Requests with no use limitation. We have inserted a new General Provisions (j): we retain all rights in our Content, Properties and data; Kubient keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables created for us are assigned to us with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. Note there is no assignment of our IP or data to Kubient, so this is a gap rather than a walk-away.

**TRANSITION (medium, missing — Section 4(c)).** On termination Kubient simply ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election — with no transition assistance, no right to receive our data back in a usable format and no deletion certification. We have inserted a new paragraph 4(c)(v) at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, expressly overriding the destroy option for Customer Data. Fallback of 90 days' assistance with export within 30 days is flagged in the comment.

**INSURANCE (low, missing — Section 14).** The Agreement contains no insurance requirement, yet Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and on its own warranty collects, maintains and stores visitor data. We have inserted a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

## Walk-away items

Three points reach or approach walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Licence revocable at will (Section 2).** An unqualified revocation right is walk-away territory; revocation must be limited to expiration or termination under Section 4.
2. **No data return on termination (Section 4(c)).** Because Kubient may elect destruction of our Confidential Information, this sits at or near the walk-away position of no data return / immediate deletion, and fails even the fallback. A machine-readable return right is required.
3. **No insurance where the vendor processes personal data (Section 14).** A hosting vendor that collects and stores visitor data with no coverage requirement is the walk-away scenario under the insurance rule.

For completeness, the uncapped direct liability under Section 7 is not itself a stated walk-away, but as a critical deviation that leaves our own exposure unlimited it should be treated as a must-fix.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the three deviations (LOL-CAP, LICENSE, RENEWAL) and the three insertions (IP ownership as General Provisions (j), transition/data return as Section 4(c)(v), insurance as Section 14(j)), with fallbacks noted in comments.
2. Confirm negotiating priority: liability cap and licence revocability first, then data return and insurance; the 90-to-30-day renewal notice is our most tradeable item (settle at 60 days).
3. **Review the Exhibits as executed.** Fee terms sit in Exhibits not included in this review. # Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Exhibit 10.14)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal (in-house counsel to Customer / AP) 
**Re:** Playbook review of the Kubient Master Services Agreement dated 5 February 
**Status:** All findings below are verified (verification: pass).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against 19 playbook rules. Thirteen clauses are compliant, three are deviations requiring redlines, and three rules have no usable clause in the document at all.

The commercial architecture is favourable to us in the areas that usually cause the most trouble. There is no exclusivity, no non-compete, no MFN, no minimum commitment, no non-solicit and no audit right running against us; Section 1 expressly confirms we remain free to offer or sell Inventory through other agents or third parties. The vendor-side indemnity at Section 11 is broad, procedurally sound and uncapped in practice, and the Section 9(b) performance warranty runs for the whole Term, which is better than our preferred position. Assignment, termination for convenience and governing law all sit at or above the fallback and are not redlined.

Three issues need to be raised with the counterparty. First, and most significant, Section 7 waives consequential damages but contains **no monetary cap of any kind**, leaving our direct liability unlimited; because this is a revenue-share deal in which we pay no fees to Kubient, a "fees paid" cap would be illusory, so we propose the greater-of formulation with a USD 1,000,000 floor plus standard uncapped carve-outs. Second, the Section 2 platform licence is expressly "revocable" without qualifier and runs to Customer alone, with Section 6(a) barring third-party access absent Kubient's prior written consent — so Affiliates and contractors are excluded and the licence could be pulled at will. Third, the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, which exceeds our 60-day fallback ceiling.

Three rules are unaddressed: there is no IP/ownership article allocating our Content, Requests or visitor data; Section 4(c) permits each party to "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information with no transition assistance or data-return right; and there is no insurance covenant at all, notwithstanding that Kubient hosts the platform and, on its own warranty, collects and stores visitor data.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | Preamble (Section 11) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | Preamble (Section 14(h)) |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | **Missing** | Preamble |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 4(a), 5) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | **Deviation** | Preamble (Sections 2, 6(a)) |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant (at fallback) | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant (law at fallback) | Preamble (Section 14(a)) |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Compliant | Preamble (Section 1) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | Preamble (Sections 1, 5) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant | Preamble |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | **Deviation** | Preamble (Section 4(a)) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 4(c)) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant (exceeds preferred) | Preamble (Sections 9(b), 13) |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | **Missing** | Preamble (Section 14) |

### Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**LOL-CAP (critical, deviation — Section 7).** Section 7 is a mutual consequential-damages waiver carved out for indemnification and breach of confidentiality, but no cap on direct liability appears anywhere in the document. The fallback requires a mutual 12-months'-fees cap with carve-outs, so the total absence of a cap fails on a material term. Our redline adds a mutual cap on the preferred greater-of basis using amounts paid or payable between the Parties with a USD 1,000,000 floor, adds the standard uncapped carve-outs, and confirms revenue-share amounts owed are not "damages" for cap purposes. The existing mutual waiver is acceptable and is left intact.

**LICENSE (high, deviation — Sections 2 and 6(a)).** The grant is expressly "revocable" with no qualifier, so on its face Kubient may withdraw the licence at will mid-Term, and it runs to "Customer" alone while Section 6(a) bars third-party access without Kubient's prior written consent — leaving Affiliate and contractor access to Kubient's discretion, contrary to the fallback (Affiliates covered on written notice). Our redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, confirms such access is not prohibited third-party access (with us responsible for their compliance), and limits revocation to expiration or termination under Section 4. Successor transfer is already handled by Section 14(h) and is preserved.

**RENEWAL (medium, deviation — Section 4(a)).** Renewal terms are successive one-year periods, which is acceptable, but the only post-Initial-Term exit is a 90-day notice, exceeding the 60-day fallback ceiling. Our redline shortens the notice to 30 days and confirms it may be exercised as a non-renewal election; we can settle at 60 days. Pricing is a revenue share with no unilateral uplift mechanic, so the CPI/3% cap is not engaged.

**IP (high, missing).** There is no ownership article. The only ownership-adjacent language is Kubient's warranty that it owns the IP in the Service, Auction Platform and products delivered, our warranty that we own the Content and Properties, and a trademark-only provision — none of which allocates ownership of our Content, Requests or visitor data, assigns deliverables, or excludes joint ownership, while Kubient collects and stores visitor data and receives Requests with no use limitation. We have inserted a new General Provisions (j): we retain all rights in our Content, Properties and data; Kubient keeps its platform and pre-existing tools; deliverables created for us are assigned to us with a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded Kubient IP; no joint ownership. Note there is no assignment of our IP or data to Kubient, so this is a gap rather than a walk-away.

**TRANSITION (medium, missing — Section 4(c)).** On termination Kubient simply ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election — with no transition assistance, no right to receive our data back in a usable format and no deletion certification. We have inserted a new paragraph 4(c)(v) at the preferred position: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification, expressly overriding the destroy option for Customer Data. Fallback of 90 days' assistance with export within 30 days is flagged in the comment.

**INSURANCE (low, missing — Section 14).** The Agreement contains no insurance requirement, yet Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and on its own warranty collects, maintains and stores visitor data. We have inserted a short covenant as new Section 14(j) at preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

## Walk-away items

Three points reach or approach walk-away territory under the playbook and should not be conceded without escalation:

1. **Licence revocable at will (Section 2).** An unqualified revocation right is walk-away territory; revocation must be limited to expiration or termination under Section 4.
2. **No data return on termination (Section 4(c)).** Because Kubient may elect destruction of our Confidential Information, this sits at or near the walk-away position of no data return / immediate deletion, and fails even the fallback. A machine-readable return right is required.
3. **No insurance where the vendor processes personal data (Section 14).** A hosting vendor that collects and stores visitor data with no coverage requirement is the walk-away scenario under the insurance rule.

For completeness, the uncapped direct liability under Section 7 is not itself a stated walk-away, but as a critical deviation that leaves our own exposure unlimited it should be treated as a must-fix.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline covering the three deviations (LOL-CAP, LICENSE, RENEWAL) and the three insertions (IP ownership as General Provisions (j), transition/data return as Section 4(c)(v), insurance as Section 14(j)), with fallbacks noted in comments.
2. Confirm negotiating priority: liability cap and licence revocability first, then data return and insurance; the 90-to-30-day renewal notice is our most tradeable item (settle at 60 days).
3. **Review the Exhibits as executed.** Fee terms sit in Exhibits not included in this review. If any Exhibit introduces an early-termination or shortfall payment by us, it should be capped at three months' fees per the LD fallback; if any Exhibit introduces committed volumes or spend, MINCOMMIT must be re-run.
4. Raise with the deal team the reporting gap noted under AUDIT: Impressions are measured solely "as measured by Kubient" and revenue share is per Exhibit with no verification right on our side. We recommend seeking a reporting/revenue-verification right in our favour — this is additive to our position rather than a deviation.
5. If drafting is reopened, align the Section 8 AAA arbitration provision with the exclusive court jurisdiction in Section 14(a). The arbitration is AAA-administered and domestic, so it does not reach the foreign-seat walk-away, and Delaware law sits at the fallback; neither point justifies a standalone redline.
